rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transaction_rows_normalized AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date AS txn_date,
    txn_amount AS txn_amount,
    txn_type AS txn_type,
    CASE
      WHEN LOWER(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      WHEN txn_amount IS NULL THEN NULL
      ELSE -txn_amount
    END AS signed_amount,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', substr(txn_date, 1, 10)) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', substr(txn_date, 1, 10)) AS INTEGER) AS month,
    substr(txn_date, 1, 10) AS txn_date_iso
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL
    AND txn_date IS NOT NULL
    AND length(trim(substr(txn_date,1,10))) = 10
    AND replace(substr(txn_date,1,10), '-', '') GLOB '[0-9]*'
),
calendar_months_range AS (
  -- build list of month starts between the min and max txn month
  SELECT
    date(min_month_start, '+' || (n) || ' months') AS month_start_date,
    date(min_month_start, '+' || (n) || ' months', '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', date(min_month_start, '+' || (n) || ' months')) AS INTEGER) AS year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', date(min_month_start, '+' || (n) || ' months')) AS INTEGER) AS month,
    n + 1 AS month_rank
  FROM (
    SELECT
      min(date(substr(txn_date_iso,1,8) || '01')) AS min_month_start,
      max(date(substr(txn_date_iso,1,8) || '01')) AS max_month_start
    FROM customer_transaction_rows_normalized
  ), (
    -- generate sequence 0..max_range where max_range is months between min and max
    SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL
    SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9 UNION ALL
    SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL
    SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19 UNION ALL
    SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL
    SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29 UNION ALL
    SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL
    SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36
  )
  WHERE date(min_month_start, '+' || n || ' months') <= (SELECT max(date(substr(txn_date_iso,1,8) || '01')) FROM customer_transaction_rows_normalized)
),
customer_monthly_closing_candidates AS (
  SELECT
    ctrn.customer_id AS customer_id,
    cmr.year AS year,
    cmr.month AS month,
    cmr.month_start_date AS month_start_date,
    cmr.month_end_date AS month_end_date,
    SUM(ctrn.signed_amount) AS net_txn_amount,
    COUNT(ctrn.customer_id) AS txn_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN lower(ctrn.txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN ctrn.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_deposits,
    SUM(CASE WHEN lower(ctrn.txn_type) <> 'deposit' THEN ctrn.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_non_deposits
  FROM calendar_months_range cmr
  LEFT JOIN customer_transaction_rows_normalized ctrn
    ON ctrn.year = cmr.year
    AND ctrn.month = cmr.month
  GROUP BY
    ctrn.customer_id,
    cmr.year,
    cmr.month,
    cmr.month_start_date,
    cmr.month_end_date
),
all_customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transaction_rows_normalized
),
customer_month_grid AS (
  SELECT c.customer_id, m.year, m.month, m.month_start_date, m.month_end_date
  FROM all_customers c
  CROSS JOIN calendar_months_range m
)
SELECT
  g.customer_id,
  g.year,
  g.month,
  g.month_start_date,
  g.month_end_date,
  -- closing_balance is cumulative sum of net_txn_amount up to this month for the customer
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(COALESCE(cm2.net_txn_amount,0))
    FROM customer_month_grid g2
    LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_closing_candidates cm2
      ON g2.customer_id = cm2.customer_id
      AND g2.year = cm2.year
      AND g2.month = cm2.month
    WHERE g2.customer_id = g.customer_id
      AND (g2.year < g.year OR (g2.year = g.year AND g2.month <= g.month))
  ), 0) AS closing_balance,
  -- monthly_change = this month's net_txn_amount
  COALESCE(cm.net_txn_amount, 0) AS monthly_change,
  -- cumulative_balance same as closing_balance (kept for clarity)
  COALESCE((
    SELECT SUM(COALESCE(cm2.net_txn_amount,0))
    FROM customer_month_grid g2
    LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_closing_candidates cm2
      ON g2.customer_id = cm2.customer_id
      AND g2.year = cm2.year
      AND g2.month = cm2.month
    WHERE g2.customer_id = g.customer_id
      AND (g2.year < g.year OR (g2.year = g.year AND g2.month <= g.month))
  ), 0) AS cumulative_balance,
  CASE WHEN COALESCE(cm.txn_count,0) = 0 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS has_activity_this_month
FROM customer_month_grid g
LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_closing_candidates cm
  ON g.customer_id = cm.customer_id
  AND g.year = cm.year
  AND g.month = cm.month
ORDER BY g.customer_id, g.year, g.month

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transactions_2020_canonical AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    CAST(strftime('%Y', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS txn_year,
    CAST(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER) AS txn_month,
    (strftime('%Y', txn_date) || '-' || strftime('%m', txn_date)) AS txn_year_month,
    CASE
      WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
      ELSE txn_amount
    END AS signed_txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
),
customer_monthly_balances_2020 AS (
  -- sum signed transactions per customer per month in 2020
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_year_month,
    txn_year,
    txn_month,
    SUM(signed_txn_amount) AS month_end_balance
  FROM customer_transactions_2020_canonical
  WHERE txn_year = 2020
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_year_month, txn_year, txn_month
),
-- For months in 2020, get count of customers with positive month-end balance and average balance across all customers for that month
monthly_positive_customer_counts_and_avg AS (
  SELECT
    txn_year_month,
    COUNT(CASE WHEN month_end_balance > 0 THEN 1 END) AS positive_customer_count,
    AVG(month_end_balance) AS average_month_end_balance
  FROM customer_monthly_balances_2020
  GROUP BY txn_year_month
)
SELECT
  high.txn_year_month AS highest_month,
  high.positive_customer_count AS highest_month_positive_customer_count,
  high.average_month_end_balance AS highest_month_average_month_end_balance,
  low.txn_year_month AS lowest_month,
  low.positive_customer_count AS lowest_month_positive_customer_count,
  low.average_month_end_balance AS lowest_month_average_month_end_balance,
  (high.average_month_end_balance - low.average_month_end_balance) AS average_difference
FROM
  (
    SELECT txn_year_month, positive_customer_count, average_month_end_balance
    FROM monthly_positive_customer_counts_and_avg
    ORDER BY positive_customer_count DESC, txn_year_month ASC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS high,
  (
    SELECT txn_year_month, positive_customer_count, average_month_end_balance
    FROM monthly_positive_customer_counts_and_avg
    ORDER BY positive_customer_count ASC, txn_year_month ASC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS low

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transaction_rows AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
    ELSE txn_amount
  END AS txn_amount_signed
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_monthly_net_txn AS (
SELECT
  ctr.customer_id AS customer_id,
  substr(ctr.txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01' AS month_start,
  SUM(ctr.txn_amount_signed) AS monthly_net_amount
FROM
  customer_transaction_rows AS ctr
GROUP BY
  ctr.customer_id,
  substr(ctr.txn_date, 1, 7) || '-01'
)
SELECT
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN g.recent_growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*),0), 6) AS percent_customers_with_recent_growth_gt_5,
  SUM(CASE WHEN g.recent_growth_rate > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS numerator_customers_with_growth_gt_5,
  COUNT(*) AS denominator_total_customers_considered,
  (SELECT MAX(month_start) FROM customer_monthly_net_txn) AS most_recent_month_considered,
  'Growth rate = (current_closing_balance - prior_closing_balance)/prior_closing_balance; if prior = 0 then growth = current_closing_balance * 100. Customers considered = those with at least one transaction month.' AS calculation_notes
FROM (
  -- compute each customer's most recent month's growth rate
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    current_month_start,
    current_closing_balance,
    COALESCE(prior_closing_balance, 0.0) AS prior_closing_balance,
    CASE
      WHEN COALESCE(prior_closing_balance, 0.0) = 0.0 THEN current_closing_balance * 100.0
      ELSE (current_closing_balance - prior_closing_balance) / prior_closing_balance
    END AS recent_growth_rate
  FROM (
    -- per-customer monthly closing balances with lag
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      month_start,
      closing_balance,
      LAG(closing_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start) AS prior_closing_balance,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start DESC) AS rn_desc,
      month_start AS current_month_start,
      closing_balance AS current_closing_balance
    FROM (
      -- cumulative sum of monthly nets to get closing balance per month
      SELECT
        customer_id,
        month_start,
        SUM(monthly_net_amount) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_start ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
      FROM customer_monthly_net_txn
    ) AS monthly_closing
  ) AS with_lag
  WHERE rn_desc = 1
) AS g

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transaction_rows AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  date(txn_date) AS txn_date_iso,
  txn_amount AS txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_monthly_cumulative_txn AS (
SELECT
  ctr.customer_id,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', ctr.txn_date_iso)) AS month_start_date,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', ctr.txn_date_iso), '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end_date,
  (SELECT SUM(ct2.txn_amount)
   FROM customer_transaction_rows ct2
   WHERE ct2.customer_id = ctr.customer_id
     AND date(ct2.txn_date_iso) <= date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', ctr.txn_date_iso), '+1 month', '-1 day')
  ) AS cumulative_txn_amount
FROM customer_transaction_rows ctr
GROUP BY ctr.customer_id, month_start_date, month_end_date
),
customer_month_start_balances_nonnegative AS (
SELECT
  m.customer_id,
  m.month_start_date,
  CASE
    WHEN m.cumulative_txn_amount < 0 THEN 0
    ELSE m.cumulative_txn_amount
  END AS balance_nonnegative
FROM customer_monthly_cumulative_txn m
)
SELECT
  m.month_start_date,
  SUM(m.balance_nonnegative) AS previous_month_total_balance
FROM customer_month_start_balances_nonnegative m
WHERE m.month_start_date > (
  SELECT MIN(strftime('%Y-%m-01', txn_date_iso)) FROM customer_transaction_rows
)
GROUP BY m.month_start_date
ORDER BY m.month_start_date ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- normalize dates and get first txn month per customer
txns AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    txn_type,
    txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date IS NOT NULL
),
first_month AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', MIN(txn_date)) AS first_ym
  FROM txns
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- daily net change per customer
daily_change AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date AS day,
    SUM(CASE WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS net_change
  FROM txns
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),
-- for each customer generate continuous calendar of days from first txn to last txn
cust_date_range AS (
  SELECT
    dc.customer_id,
    MIN(dc.day) AS min_day,
    MAX(dc.day) AS max_day
  FROM daily_change dc
  GROUP BY dc.customer_id
),
-- expand days per customer using recursive CTE
calendar AS (
  SELECT customer_id, min_day AS day, max_day
  FROM cust_date_range
  UNION ALL
  SELECT customer_id, date(day, '+1 day'), max_day
  FROM calendar
  WHERE day < max_day
),
-- left join net changes, treating missing days as zero net_change (but balance will carry forward)
daily_all AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.day,
    COALESCE(d.net_change, 0) AS net_change
  FROM calendar c
  LEFT JOIN daily_change d
    ON c.customer_id = d.customer_id AND c.day = d.day
),
-- compute running end-of-day balance per customer ordered by day
running_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    day,
    net_change,
    -- cumulative sum net_change over days
    (SELECT SUM(net_change) FROM daily_all da2
     WHERE da2.customer_id = da1.customer_id AND da2.day <= da1.day) AS end_of_day_balance
  FROM daily_all da1
),
-- prepare balances with row numbers to help windowing by date; also compute days difference to detect continuity for window fill
balances_numbered AS (
  SELECT
    rb.customer_id,
    rb.day,
    rb.end_of_day_balance,
    CAST(strftime('%s', rb.day) / 86400 AS INTEGER) AS day_seq -- integer day sequence
  FROM running_balance rb
),
-- For rolling window with carry-forward on missing days, we need continuous calendar already provided, so we can use window of 30 preceding rows (including current).
-- Compute 30-day rolling average only when at least 30 days exist for that customer up to that day.
rolling_30 AS (
  SELECT
    bn.customer_id,
    bn.day,
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY bn.customer_id ORDER BY bn.day ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) = 30
      THEN AVG(bn.end_of_day_balance) OVER (PARTITION BY bn.customer_id ORDER BY bn.day ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS avg_30
  FROM balances_numbered bn
),
-- replace negative averages with zero
rolling_30_nonneg AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    day,
    CASE WHEN avg_30 IS NOT NULL AND avg_30 < 0 THEN 0.0
         ELSE avg_30
    END AS avg_30_nn
  FROM rolling_30
),
-- tag month of each day and exclude customer's first month entirely
rolling_with_month AS (
  SELECT
    r.customer_id,
    r.day,
    strftime('%Y-%m', r.day) AS ym,
    r.avg_30_nn
  FROM rolling_30_nonneg r
  JOIN first_month f ON r.customer_id = f.customer_id
  WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', r.day) <> f.first_ym
),
-- for each customer and month get maximum avg_30_nn (ignore NULLs)
per_customer_month_max AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    ym AS month,
    MAX(avg_30_nn) AS max_30_avg
  FROM rolling_with_month
  WHERE avg_30_nn IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id, ym
),
-- sum across customers per month
monthly_sum AS (
  SELECT
    month AS month,
    SUM(max_30_avg) AS monthly_sum_max_30d_avg_balance
  FROM per_customer_month_max
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT
  month AS month,
  monthly_sum_max_30d_avg_balance
FROM monthly_sum
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transaction_daily_sums AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    SUM(txn_amount) AS daily_txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, date(txn_date)
),
customer_txn_date_span AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(MIN(txn_date)) AS min_txn_date,
    date(MAX(txn_date)) AS max_txn_date
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
max_span AS (
  SELECT CAST(MAX(julianday(max_txn_date) - julianday(min_txn_date)) AS INTEGER) AS max_days
  FROM customer_txn_date_span
),
-- generate numbers using a recursive CTE up to max_span.max_days
nums(n) AS (
  SELECT 0
  UNION ALL
  SELECT n+1 FROM nums WHERE n+1 <= (SELECT max_days FROM max_span)
),
customer_calendar AS (
  SELECT
    s.customer_id,
    date(s.min_txn_date, '+' || n.n || ' day') AS calendar_date
  FROM customer_txn_date_span s
  JOIN nums n
    ON n.n <= CAST(julianday(s.max_txn_date) - julianday(s.min_txn_date) AS INTEGER)
),
customer_daily_running_balance_prep AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.calendar_date,
    COALESCE(t.daily_txn_amount, 0) AS daily_txn_amount
  FROM customer_calendar c
  LEFT JOIN customer_transaction_daily_sums t
    ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id
   AND t.txn_date = c.calendar_date
),
-- recursive per-customer running balance computed by stepping to the next date per customer
per_customer_running AS (
  -- base rows: earliest date per customer
  SELECT
    p.customer_id,
    p.calendar_date,
    p.daily_txn_amount,
    CASE WHEN p.daily_txn_amount < 0 THEN 0 ELSE p.daily_txn_amount END AS running_balance
  FROM customer_daily_running_balance_prep p
  WHERE p.calendar_date = (
    SELECT MIN(p2.calendar_date) FROM customer_daily_running_balance_prep p2 WHERE p2.customer_id = p.customer_id
  )

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    p.customer_id,
    p.calendar_date,
    p.daily_txn_amount,
    CASE WHEN r.running_balance + p.daily_txn_amount < 0 THEN 0 ELSE r.running_balance + p.daily_txn_amount END AS running_balance
  FROM per_customer_running r
  JOIN customer_daily_running_balance_prep p
    ON p.customer_id = r.customer_id
   AND p.calendar_date = date(r.calendar_date, '+1 day')
),
customer_month_max AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(calendar_date,1,7) || '-01' AS month_year,
    MAX(running_balance) AS customer_month_max
  FROM per_customer_running
  GROUP BY customer_id, substr(calendar_date,1,7)
)
SELECT
  month_year,
  SUM(customer_month_max) AS monthly_total_max_balances
FROM customer_month_max
GROUP BY month_year
ORDER BY month_year

rows.question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH shopping_cart_event_with_names AS (
SELECT
  e.visit_id,
  e.cookie_id,
  e.page_id,
  p.product_id,
  p.page_name,
  e.event_type,
  i.event_name,
  e.sequence_number,
  e.event_time
FROM shopping_cart_events AS e
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy AS p
  ON e.page_id = p.page_id
LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier AS i
  ON e.event_type = i.event_type
),
product_event_cohort_per_visit AS (
SELECT
  scp.product_id AS product_id,
  scp.visit_id AS visit_id,
  scp.cookie_id AS cookie_id,
  scp.event_time AS event_time,
  scp.event_name AS event_name,
  scp.event_type AS event_type,
  scp.page_id AS page_id,
  scp.page_name AS page_name,
  scp.sequence_number AS sequence_number
FROM shopping_cart_event_with_names scp
JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier sei
  ON scp.event_type = sei.event_type
WHERE sei.event_name IN ('Page View','Add to Cart','Purchase')
  AND (scp.page_id IS NULL OR scp.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13))
),
product_event_counts_by_product AS (
SELECT
  scph.product_id AS product_id,
  scph.page_name AS product_name,
  SUM(CASE WHEN scph.event_name = 'Page View' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS views_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN scph.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS add_to_cart_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN scph.event_name = 'Purchase' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchase_count
FROM shopping_cart_event_with_names scph
WHERE page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
GROUP BY scph.product_id, scph.page_name
)
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_name AS product_name,
  p.views_count,
  p.add_to_cart_count,
  COALESCE(l.left_in_cart_count, 0) AS left_in_cart_count,
  p.purchase_count
FROM product_event_counts_by_product p
LEFT JOIN (
  -- compute per-product count of add-to-cart occurrences that were not followed by a purchase
  SELECT
    add_events.product_id,
    COUNT(*) AS left_in_cart_count
  FROM (
    -- each add-to-cart event (filtered to exclude unwanted page_ids in the source CTE)
    SELECT
      product_id,
      visit_id,
      cookie_id,
      event_time,
      sequence_number
    FROM product_event_cohort_per_visit
    WHERE event_name = 'Add to Cart'
      AND page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
  ) AS add_events
  LEFT JOIN (
    -- purchases for the same product and visit (or cookie) that occur after the add event
    SELECT
      product_id,
      visit_id,
      cookie_id,
      event_time AS purchase_time
    FROM product_event_cohort_per_visit
    WHERE event_name = 'Purchase'
      AND page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
  ) AS purchase_events
    ON add_events.product_id = purchase_events.product_id
    AND (
      (add_events.visit_id IS NOT NULL AND purchase_events.visit_id = add_events.visit_id)
      OR
      (add_events.visit_id IS NULL AND add_events.cookie_id IS NOT NULL AND purchase_events.cookie_id = add_events.cookie_id)
    )
    AND purchase_events.purchase_time > add_events.event_time

FROM bitcoin_transactions

  b.quantity,
  b.calendar_year
FROM bitcoin_txn_cleaned b

  CASE
    WHEN LAG(g.avg_price_per_btc_usd) OVER (PARTITION BY g.region ORDER BY g.calendar_year) IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE (g.avg_price_per_btc_usd - LAG(g.avg_price_per_btc_usd) OVER (PARTITION BY g.region ORDER BY g.calendar_year))

  -- exclude earliest year per region

rows.question: For each IPL season, identify the top three batsmen with the highest total runs scored and the top three bowlers with the most wickets taken, excluding ‘run out’, ‘hit wicket’, and ‘retired hurt’ dismissals. In the event of ties in runs or wickets, break the tie using the smaller player ID. Then output these six players in matched positions—batsman 1 with bowler 1, batsman 2 with bowler 2, and batsman 3 with bowler 3—in ascending order of the season ID, along with each player’s total runs or wickets.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH match_with_season AS (
SELECT
  match.match_id,
  match.season_id,
  match.match_date,
  match.team_1,
  match.team_2,
  match.venue
FROM match
),
wicket_events_with_bowler AS (
SELECT
  w.match_id,
  w.over_id,
  w.ball_id,
  w.innings_no,
  w.player_out,
  w.kind_out,
  b.bowler,
  m.season_id,
  b.team_bowling
FROM wicket_taken w
JOIN ball_by_ball b
  ON w.match_id = b.match_id
  AND w.over_id = b.over_id
  AND w.ball_id = b.ball_id
  AND w.innings_no = b.innings_no
JOIN match m
  ON w.match_id = m.match_id
WHERE lower(w.kind_out) NOT IN ('run out', 'hit wicket', 'retired hurt')
),
batsman_ball_runs AS (
SELECT
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.ball_id,
  b.innings_no,
  b.runs_scored,
  m.season_id,
  bb.striker,
  bb.team_batting
FROM batsman_scored b
JOIN match_with_season m ON b.match_id = m.match_id
JOIN ball_by_ball bb
  ON b.match_id = bb.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bb.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bb.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bb.innings_no
)
SELECT
  b.season_id,
  b.rank,
  b.batsman_player_id,
  bp.player_name AS batsman_player_name,
  b.batsman_total_runs,
  bw.bowler_player_id,
  bowp.player_name AS bowler_player_name,
  bw.bowler_total_wickets
FROM
  (
    SELECT season_id, striker AS batsman_player_id, total_runs AS batsman_total_runs,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY season_id ORDER BY total_runs DESC, striker ASC) AS rank
    FROM (
      SELECT season_id, striker, SUM(runs_scored) AS total_runs
      FROM batsman_ball_runs
      GROUP BY season_id, striker
    )
  ) b
JOIN
  (
    SELECT season_id, bowler AS bowler_player_id, total_wickets AS bowler_total_wickets,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY season_id ORDER BY total_wickets DESC, bowler ASC) AS rank
    FROM (
      SELECT season_id, bowler, COUNT(*) AS total_wickets
      FROM wicket_events_with_bowler
      GROUP BY season_id, bowler
    )
  ) bw
  ON b.season_id = bw.season_id AND b.rank = bw.rank
JOIN player bp ON bp.player_id = b.batsman_player_id
JOIN player bowp ON bowp.player_id = bw.bowler_player_id
WHERE b.rank <= 3
ORDER BY b.season_id ASC, b.rank ASC

rows.question: Find the IDs of players who scored the highest number of partnership runs for each match. The output should include the IDs of two players, each with their individual scores and the total partnership score. For each pair, the player with the higher individual score should be listed as player 1, and the player with the lower score as player 2. In cases where both players have the same score, the player with the higher ID should be player 1, and the player with the lower ID should be player 2. There can be multiple rows for a single match.

Calculate the total number of wickets taken by each bowler (excluding run-outs and other dismissals not attributed to the bowler), their economy rate (total runs conceded divided by total overs bowled, considering only runs scored off the bat and ignoring any extra runs like wides and no-balls), their strike rate (average number of balls bowled per wicket taken), and their best bowling performance in a single match (the match with the most wickets taken by the bowler, formatted as "wickets-runs" where runs are the runs conceded excluding extras).
rows.pred_sql:
WITH legal_delivery_runs_by_ball AS (
  SELECT
    b.match_id,
    b.over_id,
    b.ball_id,
    b.innings_no,
    b.bowler AS bowler,
    COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_off_bat,
    CASE
      WHEN er.extra_type IS NULL THEN 1
      WHEN lower(er.extra_type) IN ('wides', 'noballs') THEN 0
      ELSE 1
    END AS is_legal_delivery
  FROM ball_by_ball b
  LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
    ON bs.match_id = b.match_id
   AND bs.over_id = b.over_id
   AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id
   AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
  LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
    ON er.match_id = b.match_id
   AND er.over_id = b.over_id
   AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id
   AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
),
bowler_match_agg AS (
  SELECT
    ldrb.bowler AS bowler,
    ldrb.match_id AS match_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ldrb.is_legal_delivery = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS legal_balls_bowled,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ldrb.is_legal_delivery = 1 THEN COALESCE(ldrb.runs_off_bat, 0) ELSE 0 END) AS runs_conceded_off_bat
  FROM
    legal_delivery_runs_by_ball ldrb
  GROUP BY
    ldrb.bowler,
    ldrb.match_id
),
bowler_career_agg AS (
  SELECT
    bma.bowler AS bowler,
    SUM(bma.legal_balls_bowled) AS total_legal_balls_bowled,
    SUM(bma.runs_conceded_off_bat) AS total_runs_conceded_off_bat
  FROM bowler_match_agg bma
  GROUP BY bma.bowler
),
-- total wickets per bowler (exclude run out and NULL player_out)
wickets_per_bowler AS (
  SELECT
    bbb.bowler AS bowler,
    COUNT(*) AS total_wickets
  FROM wicket_taken wt
  JOIN ball_by_ball bbb
    ON wt.match_id = bbb.match_id
   AND wt.over_id = bbb.over_id
   AND wt.ball_id = bbb.ball_id
   AND wt.innings_no = bbb.innings_no
  WHERE wt.player_out IS NOT NULL
    AND lower(wt.kind_out) <> 'run out'
  GROUP BY bbb.bowler
),
-- wickets per bowler per match for best bowling calculation
wickets_per_bowler_match AS (
  SELECT
    bbb.bowler AS bowler,
    wt.match_id AS match_id,
    COUNT(*) AS wickets_in_match
  FROM wicket_taken wt
  JOIN ball_by_ball bbb
    ON wt.match_id = bbb.match_id
   AND wt.over_id = bbb.over_id
   AND wt.ball_id = bbb.ball_id
   AND wt.innings_no = bbb.innings_no
  WHERE wt.player_out IS NOT NULL
    AND lower(wt.kind_out) <> 'run out'
  GROUP BY bbb.bowler, wt.match_id
),
-- determine best match per bowler (most wickets, then least runs, then lowest match_id)
best_match_per_bowler AS (
  SELECT
    t.bowler,
    t.match_id,
    t.wickets_in_match,
    COALESCE(bma.runs_conceded_off_bat, 0) AS runs_in_match,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY t.bowler
      ORDER BY t.wickets_in_match DESC,
               COALESCE(bma.runs_conceded_off_bat, 0) ASC,
               t.match_id ASC
    ) AS rn
  FROM wickets_per_bowler_match t
  LEFT JOIN bowler_match_agg bma
    ON t.bowler = bma.bowler
   AND t.match_id = bma.match_id
)
SELECT
  p.player_id AS bowler,
  p.player_name,
  COALESCE(wpb.total_wickets, 0) AS total_wickets,
  CASE 
    WHEN bca.total_legal_balls_bowled = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (bca.total_runs_conceded_off_bat * 6.0) / bca.total_legal_balls_bowled
  END AS economy_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(wpb.total_wickets,0) = 0 THEN NULL
    WHEN bca.total_legal_balls_bowled = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE bca.total_legal_balls_bowled * 1.0 / wpb.total_wickets
  END AS strike_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN bmpb.wickets_in_match IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(bmpb.wickets_in_match AS TEXT) || '-' || CAST(bmpb.runs_in_match AS TEXT)
  END AS best_bowling
FROM bowler_career_agg bca
JOIN player p ON p.player_id = bca.bowler
LEFT JOIN wickets_per_bowler wpb ON wpb.bowler = bca.bowler
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT bowler, match_id, wickets_in_match, runs_in_match
  FROM best_match_per_bowler
  WHERE rn = 1
) bmpb ON bmpb.bowler = bca.bowler
ORDER BY p.player_name

rows.question: List the bowlers (including their ID, first name, and last name), match number, game number, handicap score, tournament date, and location for only those bowlers who have won games with a handicap score of 190 or less at all three venues: Thunderbird Lanes, Totem Lanes, and Bolero Lanes. Only include the specific game records where they won with a handicap score of 190 or less at these three locations.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH tournament_matches_with_tourney AS (
SELECT
  TM.MatchID,
  TM.TourneyID,
  TM.Lanes,
  TM.OddLaneTeamID,
  TM.EvenLaneTeamID,
  T.TourneyDate,
  T.TourneyLocation
FROM Tourney_Matches TM
LEFT JOIN Tournaments T
  ON TM.TourneyID = T.TourneyID
),
bowler_game_results AS (
SELECT
  bs.MatchID,
  bs.GameNumber,
  bs.BowlerID,
  bs.RawScore,
  bs.HandiCapScore,
  bs.WonGame,
  b.BowlerFirstName,
  b.BowlerLastName,
  tm.TourneyID,
  t.TourneyDate,
  t.TourneyLocation
FROM Bowler_Scores AS bs
JOIN Bowlers AS b
  ON bs.BowlerID = b.BowlerID
JOIN Tourney_Matches AS tm
  ON bs.MatchID = tm.MatchID
JOIN Tournaments AS t
  ON tm.TourneyID = t.TourneyID
),
bowler_winning_games_by_location AS (
SELECT
  bgr.BowlerID,
  bgr.TourneyLocation,
  MIN(bgr.HandiCapScore) AS min_HandiCapScore,
  COUNT(*) AS winning_games_count
FROM
  bowler_game_results bgr
WHERE
  bgr.WonGame = 1
GROUP BY
  bgr.BowlerID,
  bgr.TourneyLocation
)
SELECT
  bgr.BowlerID,
  bgr.BowlerFirstName,
  bgr.BowlerLastName,
  bgr.MatchID,
  bgr.GameNumber,
  bgr.HandiCapScore,
  bgr.TourneyDate,
  bgr.TourneyLocation
FROM bowler_game_results bgr
JOIN (
  SELECT BowlerID
  FROM bowler_winning_games_by_location
  WHERE TourneyLocation IN ('Thunderbird Lanes','Totem Lanes','Bolero Lanes')
    AND winning_games_count > 0
    AND min_HandiCapScore <= 190
  GROUP BY BowlerID
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT TourneyLocation) = 3
) qualified ON bgr.BowlerID = qualified.BowlerID
WHERE bgr.WonGame = 1
  AND bgr.HandiCapScore <= 190
  AND bgr.TourneyLocation IN ('Thunderbird Lanes','Totem Lanes','Bolero Lanes')
ORDER BY bgr.BowlerID ASC, bgr.TourneyDate ASC, bgr.MatchID ASC, bgr.GameNumber ASC
